newsitem.title: USA: US wheat flour export subsidies still under review.
newsitem.headline: US wheat flour export subsidies still under review.

text.p: The Clinton administration is still mulling where to revive export subsidies for wheat flour and barley malt, a top U.S. official said Tuesday.
"It's still being considered," U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman told reporters after a ceremony to swear in a new team of USDA undersecretaries.
The idea is "not dead gone and gone," despite the delay in winning interagency approval, he said.
Glickman first acknowledged nearly a month ago that the administration was considering whether to renew wheat flour and barley malt export subsidies to help regain lost market share.
U.S. exports of both commodities have suffered in recent year due to subsidized competition from the European Union.
Despite that, some other administration agencies question whether export subsidies for either commodity are warranted, USDA aides have said.

The same skeptics have also expressed concern that reviving wheat flour and barley malt export subsidies could lead to the much bigger step of subsidizing U.S. wheat flour exports for the first time in more than two years, the aides said.
The new team sworn in on Tuesday includes Gus Schumacher, undersecretary for farm and foreign agricultural services.
One of Schumacher's first jobs will be to analyze the trade competition facing U.S. farmers, focusing particularlly on the actions of the European Union, Glickman said.
